NEPA requires the statement to include a discussion of unavoidable adverse effects, alternatives, effects on long-term productivity, and irreversible commitments of resources which are involved in the proposed action. In order to satisfy the requirements of NEPA, and to effectively implement the purposes of the Executive Order, the draft statement on off-road vehicles should identify clearly the values that deserve protection on the public lands and document precisely the impact of ORV use on those values.
Unfortunately, the Draft Statement fails completely to carry out the clear mandate of NEPA and E.O. 11644. It is a nebulous document that only confuses and weakens Interior's attempt to fulfill its responsibilities. As a result, it seriously misdirects the effort to preserve and enhance environmental quality on the public lands. This comment will discuss the deficiencies that make the Draft Statement so weak, and will suggest a new approach for a more forthright policy of environmental protection.
II. Defects of the Draft Statement
A. Failure to indicate the proposal which it accompanies.
According to the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), sec. 102(2)(c), an impact statement must "accompany" proposals for "major Federal actions significantly affecting the quality of the environment."
